name: Heel slide
equipment: a smooth floor or a towel under the heel
movement: lying on the back, one heel slid toward the buttock and back out

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where your legs will be.

words.hint: Lying on your back, one heel slid along the floor toward you, bending the knee, then back out.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie on your back side on to it, both legs straight.
words.position: Lie on your back, side on to the phone, both legs straight, the working leg nearest the camera. A towel under the heel helps it slide.
words.top: The heel slid in toward the buttock as far as is comfortable — the knee bent to about a right angle — the heel and the hips on the floor.
howto: Lie on your back, legs straight, hips and shoulders on the floor.
Slide the heel of the working leg along the floor toward your buttock, bending the knee as far as is comfortable. Keep the heel on the floor.
Hold at the deepest point for the count. Hips still on the floor.
Slide the heel back out until the leg is straight. The rep counts there.
words.cannot: The feel inside the knee and the stretch at the front of the thigh: it sees the knee angle, the hips and the heel.
words.about: Heel slide — lying on the back side on: the knee angle, from 180 straight; the rep is under way once it is under 150 and counts when the leg is back past 165; the target at the deepest point is at most 90° (a right angle), which is the first goal after knee surgery — most daily life needs 90–110, a bike 110–120 — and the setting to move as the knee frees; the hips on the floor, as the hip no more than 8° above the shoulder; and the heel on the floor, no more than 10° above the other heel. Hold two seconds at the deepest point.
words.lost: Lie down side on to the camera, hips to feet in the picture
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Go to firm stretch, not sharp pain. After surgery, follow the range your surgeon or physio has set.
words.easier: A shallower bend; a shorter hold; a slippery surface under the heel.
words.harder: A deeper bend; a longer hold; a strap round the ankle to help the last few degrees.
words.mistakes: Lifting the heel off the floor; lifting the hip to help the knee bend; rushing the slide back out; holding the breath.

measurements.label: knee bend
measurements.why: The knee angle: 180 straight, 90 a right angle. Also the progress measurement: under way under raiseAt, back out past downAt. The target falls as the knee frees.

settings.label: Knee angle at the deepest point, at most (90 is a right angle)

measurements.label: hip above the shoulder
measurements.why: The shoulder-to-hip line off level: the hip coming up to help the knee bend.

settings.label: Hip above the shoulder, at most (degrees)

measurements.label: heel above the other heel
measurements.why: The heel lifting off the floor as it slides, against the other heel. Not read when the other heel is hidden.

settings.label: Heel above the other heel, at most (degrees)

faults.label: Slide further
faults.text: Slide the heel further toward you
faults.deep: Further in if you can — bend the knee a little more

faults.label: Hip lifting
faults.text: Keep the hips on the floor
faults.deep: The hip is coming up — press it down and slide the heel less far

faults.label: Heel lifting
faults.text: Keep the heel on the floor as it slides

settings.label: Knee angle that counts as under way
